features.name: Dashboard session hardening
features.note: The opaque session cookie is re-keyed every 15 minutes on a safe GET, and the old value is dead immediately; an idle session (default 30 minutes, `WEB_SESSION_IDLE_MS`, minimum 1 minute) is refused and its row deleted, while activity inside the window moves `last_seen_at` without extending the absolute 7-day lifetime; an expired Discord access token is refreshed from a sealed refresh token, rotated in the same write, with one in-flight refresh per session so two concurrent requests spend the token once; logout revokes the sealed refresh grant before deleting the row; fixed-window limits cover the auth, dashboard, write and API classes with Retry-After; and WEB_OWNER_IDS gates the instance console and its sign-out-everywhere action. Live 2026-11-03 over real local HTTP and Postgres (`web-session-idle-refresh`, `web-session-hardening`). Revocation and refresh are asserted at the fake OAuth port because the probe's exchange is fake; no live Discord login, revocation or refresh is claimed.

features.name: Config templates
features.note: Three built-in templates and named saved templates share one plan: a patch or snapshot is deep-merged over each guild's current settings, parsed by that module's own Zod schema and diffed before anything is written. Apply is bound to a SHA-256 fingerprint of the displayed plan, re-authorizes every selected guild, refuses a missing/stale preview and writes through SettingsService with one dashboard audit row per module. A saved template is a guild-owned snapshot (migration 0016) with in-memory and Drizzle adapters; an out-of-validity stored row is reported and refused at 400. Create/update/delete are audited. Live over real local HTTP on Postgres with two guilds.

features.note: A guild's effective module settings download as a checksummed JSON file; import parses and schema-validates the file, previews the exact diff, and applies only with a matching SHA-256 fingerprint, writing through SettingsService with one dashboard audit row per module. The applied bundle becomes the guild's baseline, and the drift page compares baseline to live. Saved templates are the sibling slice: one snapshot per guild, applied through this same fingerprint and audit path.

features.name: Scoped API tokens
features.note: One `ApiTokenStore` port with in-memory and Drizzle adapters (migration 0018). A `keystone_…` secret is shown once by the dashboard and only its SHA-256 hash is stored; a token is bound to one guild and a subset of guild:read, analytics:read and settings:write. Bearer authentication feeds the same `/api/v1` handlers as a session, checks guild and scope per route and gives each token its own fixed window. Issue and revoke pass the guild write gate and append one api_token.issue/api_token.revoke dashboard audit row. `/api/v1/openapi.json` is generated from an operation table that a route-drift test checks both ways. Live 2026-11-03 over real local HTTP on Postgres.

features.name: Public API / webhooks
features.note: Webhook subscriptions and signed delivery plus `Idempotency-Key` replay on the token principal. One `WebhookStore` port has in-memory and Drizzle adapters over `webhook_subscriptions` and `webhook_deliveries` (migration 0019); the signing secret is `whsec_…`, shown once and stored sealed, and every delivery carries `t=<unix>,v1=<hmac>` over `<t>.<body>` so a receiver can reject a forged or stale body. Delivery is an outbox row written before the network call: three attempts with exponential backoff, then a terminal failed receipt the admin reads on the page. Settings updates and token issue/revoke enqueue events; the drainer lives in the web process because it already owns the sealing key. `Idempotency-Key` reuses `PostgresIdempotencyStore`/`job_receipts`: the same key and body replay the stored status and exact response bytes, a different body is `409`, and only the first call writes. Creating, testing and removing an endpoint pass the session -> guild -> CSRF gate and append dashboard audit rows. Live 2026-11-03 over real local HTTP on Postgres: a local receiver verified the HMAC independently, an always-500 receiver was retried three times then failed, the receipt page showed the 500, and the replay/conflict cases held.

features.name: i18n
features.note: One framework-free `packages/i18n` instead of i18next: message keys are typed from the English catalog, so a translation must accept the same arguments and cannot drop an interpolation or change a plural argument's type. `en` and a hand-written `de` cover the surfaces that ship (the form panel and its modal/review receipts, the component-router refusals and the ping/about/form command descriptions); an untranslated key falls back to English, then to a plain sentence, never the raw key. The per-guild locale is `setup.locale`, an enum validated by the setup module's own Zod schema through the one SettingsService write path, so `/config`, the dashboard widget and the API share it; an unsupported value is refused and the effective locale stays. Discord command descriptions carry locale maps generated from the same catalog, and an untranslated command stays English-only. The rest of the modules' copy is not translated yet. Live 2026-11-03 through the real discord.js adapter on Postgres.
